hints.content:
$f$ is increasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $f(x)$ also increases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going upwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by zero point five. The graph of y equals f of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through a local maximum at the point negative four point seven-five, one and decreases to the local minimum and x-intercept at negative three, zero. Then it increases to a local maximum at negative one point five, one. Then it decreases to a local minimum and x-intercept at zero point one, zero. Then is increases to a local maximum at one point six, one. Then in decreases to a local minimum and x-intercept at three point two, zero. Then it increases to a local maximum at four point eight, one. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative three to x equals negative one point five, from x equals zero point one to x equals one point six, and from x equals three point two to x equals four point eight.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $f$ increasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-3<x<-2$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$-1<x<0$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $f$ is decreasing on this interval
$3.5<x<4.5$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
